summary: Reproduced both LlamaForCausalLM startup crashes on the actual serving path and added early argument/model validation rejecting --enable-multi-layer-eagle for ordinary Llama checkpoints before weights or draft workers are loaded.

tests.command: python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py -k 'TestMultiLayerEagleArgs and rejects_llama' (with source patch reversed)
tests.what_was_measured: The regression failed before the fix because no ValueError was raised.
The new rejection and two boundary cases passed: ordinary Llama EAGLE retains (5,4,8), and MiMoV2 multi-layer EAGLE retains (3,1,4).
On gfx950, target weights loaded and startup reproduced the reported (8,5) MultiLayerEagleDraftWorker assertion. Raw log: evidence/before-server.log.
On gfx950, startup passed the invariant and reproduced the reported unexpected draft_model_idx constructor keyword. Raw log: evidence/before-explicit-server.log.
The real launch path rejected LlamaForCausalLM during argument resolution with the intended clear ValueError, before weight loading. Raw log: evidence/after-server.log.

remaining_limitations: The deterministic two-layer random Llama fixture validates the serving startup and GPU model-loading path only; it does not establish TinyLlama semantic accuracy or full-model behavior.

No embedded-MTP model weights were available, so supported multi-layer EAGLE runtime generation was not exercised; its existing configuration behavior is covered by an independent MiMoV2 boundary test.
The fix intentionally addresses ordinary LlamaForCausalLM only and does not attempt a general capability registry for every model architecture.
